launcher: Button prompts now cover the Pokémon selection screen before a battle, not only Quick moves, and an arrow key shows as a bold arrow.

Online: with team preview you now pick your Pokémon in the game, on Battle Mode's own selection screen with its music, instead of in the launcher. You have 90 seconds, then the first of your party go. Both players need this launcher.

Choose starters: a New Game can begin with any two Pokémon instead of Espeon and Umbreon, picked in the game after you enter your name. It's on by default; turn it off under Gameplay to skip the question.

Fixed the team builder offering only the moves a Pokémon learns in Colosseum: it now lists every move it can learn in Generation 3, as Pokémon Showdown does, with move tutor, Ruby and Sapphire, FireRed and LeafGreen, XD and event moves, and says how each is learned.

Online timers: a turn timer gives each player up to 99 seconds a choice, and when it runs out the game chooses for them, as Battle Mode does; a battle timer ends the battle after its minutes, won by whoever has more Pokémon left, then more HP. Set them under Turn timer and Battle timer when you create a room: Orre Colosseum, Hoenn Stadium and Gen 3 OU have a minute a turn and 20 minutes a battle (30 for Gen 3 OU), Casual none unless you choose. A player whose game stops choosing loses, and the room list shows a room's timers. Both players need this launcher.

Online formats take only legal Pokémon: in Orre Colosseum, Hoenn Stadium and Gen 3 OU, each move has to be one the Pokémon could learn in the third generation (by level, TM, move tutor, egg or event), its held item one a Pokémon can hold, and its EVs and IVs in range, checked when you create a room and when you join one, with what's wrong said. A host can allow them by turning off Only legal Pokémon under Customise.

Team builder: with Platinum's rules chosen under Rules on the Online page, each move shows as physical or special by itself, as it battles, not by its type: Shadow Ball is special and Hidden Power always special.
Online: a room of any format, Casual too, can play by Pokémon Platinum's battle rules. Choose Platinum's under Rules when you create the room, and both players battle by them; the room list says so.
Fixed Generation 4 rules taking away an ability whose name Colosseum runs together, such as Rhydon's and Manectric's Lightning Rod.

Pokémon packs: add Pokémon of your own making, new ones or forms of the game's, with their own name, stats, types, moves and TMs, evolutions, model and sprites. Press Open Pokémon packs folder in the Pokédex, where they show after the Pokémon they're based on, with who made them.

Later generations, under Settings → Gameplay: play by Pokémon Platinum's battle rules, where Metronome can call Generation 4's moves too, and add the 107 Generation 4 Pokémon and their moves to your game (with their own abilities under Platinum's rules) and the Pokédex.

Battle Revolution models: turning on Generation 4 Pokémon asks for your own Pokémon Battle Revolution disc, and choosing it makes their models and icons from it, with how many are made shown as it goes. No Blender needed. Without it, a Colosseum Pokémon stands in for each one's looks; add the disc later under Settings → Gameplay.
Save backups now keep your PC's boxes 4 to 10 with your save, and exporting a save for Dolphin tells you when Pokémon in those boxes stay behind, as Dolphin's game has only 3 boxes.
Show shiny Shadow Pokémon and Shiny starters: switches for the game's new shiny options, both on to start with. Find them under Gameplay.

Language: play in French, German, Spanish or Italian, with the European release's text, menus, battle screens and colosseum title cards. Choose it under Settings → Gameplay; it downloads the first time you play with it. A fan translation works too: put its folder in the languages folder (Open languages folder) and it shows in the list.

Fixed the game drawing with OpenGL instead of Vulkan on a Steam Deck and other Linux PCs with a newer Mesa: Vulkan found no graphics card because the game got the build tools' older copy of a graphics library. It now starts with your system's own copy.

Game Boy Advance: link your Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire, Emerald, FireRed or LeafGreen save to the game, as with the GCN-GBA cable, to register your team for Colosseum Battle, trade Pokémon with it, and spend its Poké Coupons on prizes. Choose the save under Settings → Game Boy Advance, which also finds the ones your emulators keep and says if one isn't ready to link. No GBA BIOS or Game Pak is needed; if linking from the save doesn't work for your game, Advanced runs the GBA itself from a dump of the Game Pak instead. A copy of the save is kept before each session.

Windows: the game's program now has its icon, Espeon and Umbreon from the game's memory card, taken from your disc when the game builds. The build log no longer shows an error about a missing main.dol.

Team builder: give each Pokémon in a party its own moves, held item, ability, nature, EVs, IVs, nickname, gender and shininess, with its stats worked out as you go and the moves it can learn in this game. Bring teams in or out as Pokémon Showdown text, or copy your Story party into a party of your own to change. Open it with New party or Edit on the Online tab.

HD textures: the ground, walls and floors keep their grain instead of coming out flat, such as Agate Village's grass, Pyrite Town's dirt and the sand outside the Mystery Lab, with no bright or dark lines between tiles. Move effects keep their soft edges: Yawn's glow no longer has a hard rim and a black dot, Shock Wave's sparks are no longer hard needles, and Thunder Wave's and Confusion's rings and swirls are soft again. Also fixed black lines in some floors and furniture, such as Pyrite's metal floors and the shelves and stairs in Miror B.'s building, and dark edges on some textures, such as black at the base of Pikachu's ears. The updated pack, about 1.9 GB, downloads the next time you play with HD textures on and replaces the old one, and a download of an earlier pack that stopped partway is deleted.

Windows: if the folder for Setup files has an & in its path, the launcher now says so before building and explains how to choose another folder. Before, the game failed to build near the end, with "ar.exe: … No such file or directory" in the activity log.

Online formats: create a room as Orre Colosseum (doubles, bring 6 pick 4), Hoenn Stadium (singles, pick 3) or Gen 3 OU (Smogon's 6-on-6), with their clauses and bans, or keep Casual, the rooms as they were. Customise changes any rule, and the room list shows a named variant such as Orre Limited, or Orre Colosseum* (custom) with what changed. Games makes a room a best of 3 or 5 with the same party for the set, and with team preview both players see both parties and pick before each game. A room your party can't play says why. Choose them under Create room on the Online tab.

Randomizer: with Generation 4 Pokémon turned on, a randomized run can have them too, as starters, Shadow Pokémon, trainers' Pokémon and gifts. Choose Gen 4 beside the other generations under Randomizer; No legendaries leaves out Generation 4's legendaries too.
Fixed Generation 4 Pokémon that don't evolve evolving as the Pokémon standing in for their looks does, such as Arceus into Linoone at level 20.

Pokédex: with HD textures on and downloaded, the 3D models and the Pokémon's pictures use them, as the game does, so faces, eyes and markings are sharp. Custom textures you've added show there too, and the team builder's pictures get the HD ones as well.

Fixed Generation 4 Pokémon's faces from Battle Revolution sitting small inside a grey ring in the battle and menu frames, with the scene showing through the corners: they now fill the frame as the game's own faces do.
Battle Revolution models: when a fix changes models you've already made, Settings → Gameplay says how many, and Make models makes only those again.
Generation 4 rules: Astonish, Extrasensory and Needle Arm no longer do double damage to a Pokémon that used Minimize, as in Platinum.
Online battles: both players need this update of the launcher, as it changes Generation 4's move data. Joining a room from another version of the launcher says so.
Pokédex: Battle Revolution models show and hide parts as they move, such as Honchkrow folding its wings, as they do in battle.
When a fix changes your Battle Revolution models, a warning above Play says so, and its Make models button makes them again.

Generation 4 Pokémon, under Settings → Gameplay: the game's own Pokémon now learn their moves and evolve as in Pokémon Platinum, so Yanma, Aipom and Piloswine can become Yanmega, Ambipom and Mamoswine, and Murkrow, Misdreavus, Sneasel, Gligar and the rest reach their Generation 4 forms by level where the game has no stone or trade item for them. The Pokédex shows those evolutions.

Fixed Generation 4 Pokémon evolving by the wrong rules: a male Combee no longer becomes Vespiquen, Burmy becomes Wormadam or Mothim by its gender, Riolu, Budew and Chingling evolve by friendship, and Bonsly and Mime Jr. evolve by knowing Mimic, Mantyke with a Remoraid in the party and Happiny at level 25, instead of all at level 36.
Generation 4 Pokémon learn the moves Pokémon Platinum teaches them by level, not ones from HeartGold and SoulSilver.

Quick moves: in battle, press Z (R1 or RB, the right bumper, on other controllers) to open your moves (the battle menu shows that button beside FIGHT), each shown with its button, then A, B, X or Y to use the first, second, third or fourth move at once, as in Pokémon Stadium. The buttons look like the controller or keyboard you're using, as you've bound them; choose another look under Controls → Button prompts. Quick status effects: a status condition or stat change shows right where the move hit, without its own camera shot, and the battle moves on once its message closes. Turn them on under Gameplay.
When the game stops itself after an error, the launcher's message says why, in the game's own words, instead of only its exit code.
game: Fixed the arrow keys picking nothing on the Pokémon selection screen before a battle: on a keyboard, the arrows and WASD now pick as the Control Pad does. The screen also shows your own keys or your controller's buttons beside each Pokémon and for Cancel and Check, as set under Controls → Button prompts.

Online battles now have Battle Mode's screens around them: both trainers and their Pokémon with the VS before the battle, and the results after it with each Pokémon's HP and who won. Press A on the results to go back to the launcher.

Choose your starters: after you enter your name for a New Game, the game asks whether to begin with Espeon and Umbreon. Say No to pick any two Pokémon from a grid of their faces in alphabetical order, with a row of letters to jump between (L and R), and each one's number, types and level shown; they start at Umbreon's and Espeon's levels with the moves they know there. Generation 4 Pokémon can be picked too when they're turned on.

Online battles can have Battle Mode's choice and battle timers, shown on screen as in Battle Mode, with both games keeping the battle's time alike so the battle ends on the same turn for both. A battle that runs out of time with both sides even is a draw.
Pokémon from your Pokémon packs appear in the game with their own names, stats, moves, models, shiny models, face icons and PC sprites. Nothing in the game hands them out yet.

Generation 4 battle rules as Pokémon Platinum plays them: its damage, critical hits, accuracy and turn order, moves physical or special by themselves, Waterfall's chance to flinch, Volt Tackle's to paralyze, Acid lowering Sp. Def and Crunch Defense, the game's Pokémon with the abilities Platinum gives them (Scizor's Technician, Breloom's Poison Heal), Generation 4's moves after the game's own, each doing what it does in Platinum, Generation 4's held items such as Life Orb, Focus Sash, Choice Scarf and Light Clay, Berries eaten as soon as HP drops far enough, and room for far more than 25 new Pokémon.
Fixed a number showing instead of the move's name when a Pokémon forgets a move in battle to learn a new one, such as "Umbreon forgot 25" for Taunt.
Fixed the sandstorm, and the strong sunlight after Sunny Day, stopping short of the sides in widescreen: they now cover the whole screen, with the sandstorm's clouds at their usual size.
Fixed the PDA leaving black bars, or the room behind it, at the sides in widescreen: its green background and scanlines now fill the screen.
Fixed the name screen, where you choose your name at the start of Story Mode, leaving a black bar at the left side in widescreen: its blue stripes now fill the screen.
Randomizer: fixed the PDA's Snag List showing the original game's Shadow Pokémon, such as Makuhita named as Duskull, instead of the ones your run gave you.

Shiny Shadow Pokémon: a Shadow Pokémon that will be shiny once you snag it now looks shiny in battle, with the shiny sparkle as it comes out. Before, how it looked in battle didn't match the Pokémon you got. Whether it's shiny is decided when you first meet it in battle, and it stays the same if you lose or battle it again; only resetting to a save from before you met it gives a new chance. Espeon and Umbreon can now be shiny too, at 1 in 8192 as in other Pokémon games, from a New Game.

Language packs: the game can play in another language from a pack of its text, its menu pictures and the letters its fonts lack. The launcher sets this up; without it, start the game with COLO_LANGUAGE set to a pack's folder.
Linking a Game Boy Advance from a save now connects in a few seconds, instead of keeping you waiting while the game sent the GBA its program.
Fixed the game failing to build on Macs with Xcode 26, with "ld: Missing -platform_version option" in the activity log.

Game Boy Advance: the game links with a Gen 3 Pokémon save on controller socket 2, answering as the GBA would, and writes trades and coupon prizes back into it. In a trade your controller also works the GBA's side. With a Game Pak too, mGBA runs the GBA itself, as in Dolphin, with its screen in a corner and its sound mixed in: press G (Back on a controller) to use it and again to go back, hold it to turn the GBA on or off, and drop an e-Reader card's file on the window to scan it.

Fixed setup failing near the end when the game's Vulkan parts couldn't be downloaded from GitHub: the game now builds anyway and draws with OpenGL, and a build that fails at its last step says why in the activity log.
Fixed coloured text showing the wrong colour: the gold Name, Play Time and Snagged POKéMON labels on the save and Continue screens were red.

The PC now has 10 boxes instead of 3, room for 300 Pokémon. L and R go through all ten, and a Pokémon sent to the PC goes to the first box with room. Boxes 4 to 10 are kept beside your save, so the save still opens in Dolphin, with boxes 1 to 3.
Online battles now have critical hits, and Latias and Latios get Soul Dew's boost, as in the original game's link battles. Before, neither happened online.

Online battles can be double battles, and can play by the original game's Battle Mode clauses: sleep, freeze, self-KO (Selfdestruct or Explosion loses a tie) and no Perish Song or Destiny Bond from a last Pokémon, with the other player's HP shown as a bar only if the room asks.
The randomizer can choose Generation 4 Pokémon for a new run when the launcher adds them. Runs started before play as they always have.

Fixed Burmy's model from Battle Revolution coming apart when it moved, with its head at the bottom and its leaves stretched into tall blades, and smaller mistakes in how Shieldon's, Purugly's and Hippopotas's models bend.
Fixed the battle camera aiming at the ground under most Generation 4 Pokémon from Battle Revolution when a move hit them, which cut tall ones like Garchomp off at the head.
Fixed the game closing when Heal Block or Captivate was used in a double battle under Generation 4 rules.

Generation 4 rules in double battles: Surf, Discharge and Lava Plume now hit both foes and your partner, and Earthquake, Magnitude, Selfdestruct and Explosion do three quarters of their damage when they hit more than one Pokémon, as in Platinum. Acupressure can be aimed at your partner; aimed at a foe, it raises your own stat.

Fixed held items under Generation 4 rules: Leftovers healed after every move instead of once a turn, and a move that hits several times, or several Pokémon, stopped doing damage once its target's Berry or Leftovers went off.

Fixed more held items under Generation 4 rules: Life Orb and Shell Bell acted after every hit instead of once a move, the Metronome item and Zoom Lens did nothing, and Berries are now also eaten as a Pokémon comes out and after poison or burn damage at the end of a turn.

Fixed moves being stopped by an immunity that Generation 4 lifts: Ground moves now hit a Pokémon that used Roost, is under Gravity or holds an Iron Ball, Psychic moves hit a Dark type after Miracle Eye, Scrappy's Normal and Fighting moves hit Ghosts, Normalize makes every move act as Normal, and Mold Breaker gets past Levitate, Wonder Guard and Soundproof.

Fixed Generation 4 moves that didn't match Platinum: Copycat always failed, Rapid Spin left Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes, Baton Pass dropped Magnet Rise, Aqua Ring, Power Trick, Gastro Acid, Heal Block and Embargo, and Take Down and Submission cost a quarter of the user's own HP.

More Generation 4 moves now match Platinum: Grass Knot and Low Kick go by weight in kilograms, Healing Wish and Lunar Dance heal after the entry hazards, Payback is doubled against a Pokémon that just switched in, confusion damage varies, and Fling, Pluck, Bug Bite, Last Resort, Trump Card, Worry Seed, Psych Up, Camouflage, Secret Power and Razor Wind have smaller fixes.

Fixed Generation 4 abilities that didn't match Platinum: Tangled Feet did nothing, Magic Guard didn't stop recoil, full paralysis or a missed Jump Kick's crash, Slow Start lasted a turn too long for a Pokémon that started the battle, and Leaf Guard didn't stop Yawn in the sun.

More Generation 4 abilities now match Platinum: Will-O-Wisp sets off Flash Fire, Lightning Rod and Storm Drain draw Hidden Power, Pressure makes weather and other field moves cost extra PP, and Anticipation, Forewarn, Download and Trace have smaller fixes.

Fixed Generation 4 Pokémon models from Battle Revolution: Glameow's tail and Buneary's ears no longer stretch, Bonsly's feet, Spiritomb's spirits and Purugly's tail stay where they belong, Honchkrow, the Starly line, Darkrai, Rotom and Shaymin show the right one of their two wings, bodies, hands or flowers, Froslass and Munchlax have their eyes, and see-through wings and petals are see-through. Press Make models under Settings → Gameplay to make them again.
Fixed the game failing to build on computers with pandoc, markdown or kramdown installed, as many Macs have, with "cannot create target README" in the activity log.

With Generation 4 Pokémon, a Pokémon evolves by knowing a move (Yanma, Aipom, Piloswine, Tangela, Lickitung), with another Pokémon in the party (Mantyke) or by level for one gender (Kirlia into Gallade, Snorunt into Froslass, Burmy, Combee), as in Pokémon Platinum.

With Generation 4 Pokémon, the Move Deleter in Mt. Battle's Pokémon Center can also make a Pokémon remember a move it learns by level up to its level, so a Shadow Pokémon caught past the level it learns a move at can still evolve by knowing it.

Battles can open the moves with one button, Z (the right bumper on other controllers), shown beside FIGHT, each move shown with its button as your controller or keyboard has it, and use one with A, B, X or Y, and can show status conditions and stat changes without their own camera shot and the wait after them.

Fixed the game crashing at start-up, with no reason given, when it couldn't read part of its disc file (as with a disc in OneDrive that can't be downloaded) or the disc had been changed by another tool. It now says which, and what to do.
Fixed PlayStation controllers, such as the DualSense, stopping in the game on Windows a few seconds after it started, even though they worked in the launcher.
Randomizer: a Shadow Pokémon or trainer's Pokémon that held the item for its own type, such as Shadow Quilava's Charcoal, now holds the one for its new species' type.
Fixed Shadow Rush doing no damage to Ghost-type Pokémon with Generation 4 battle rules.
Fixed Hippopotas, Luxio, Shellos, Riolu, Tangrowth, Glaceon and Gallade from Battle Revolution not reacting when hit. Press Make models under Settings → Gameplay to make them again.
Fixed move sounds such as Sing, Attract and Captivate having a dull echo trailing behind them that the original game doesn't have.
Fixed a stretched box around Sweet Scent's and Confusion's ripple in widescreen.

launcher: Online battles: open a room or join one on the new Online tab and battle another player, at level 50 or 100 with 3 or 6 Pokémon each. Build named parties of six from your Pokédex, and your game waits in the stadium until someone joins. The room list updates by itself, and Refresh checks right away.

Story party: battle online with the Pokémon you travel with. The Online tab shows the party in your save, set apart at the top, and brings each one along with its moves, nature, stats, ability, held item and nickname, at the room's level. A party of 3 to 5 can take rooms of 3 each, and Shadow Pokémon stay home until they're purified.
The top bar shows how many players are online. It comes from an anonymous check-in you can turn off under Settings → Launcher.

Show on Discord: while you play, your Discord profile shows where you are in Orre with a picture of the place, who you're battling and your lead Pokémon, and online battles show your opponent. The Discord app needs to be open. Turn it off under Settings → Launcher.

Pokédex: browse all 386 Pokémon from your own disc, turn their 3D models around, play their motions and see their shiny looks. It also shows how you can get each one, and locks those the game keeps out of reach. Find it in the new Pokédex tab.

Randomizer: start a New Game with different starters, Shadow Pokémon, trainers' Pokémon and gifts, chosen by a seed you can share. Limit it to the generations you like, keep Pokémon about as strong as those they replace, or leave legendaries out. Your save keeps its seed, so fights stay the same when you try again. Find it under Gameplay.
Export a save: carry on in Dolphin with a .gci file of your game. Find it in the Saves tab.
Battle animations: a speed slider from 1× to 5× in steps of 0.1, with 1.5× as the new default, and a Skip battle animations switch that greys it out. Find them under Gameplay.

Macs with Apple Silicon: the game now builds as a native program and draws with Metal, so it runs faster and Rosetta is no longer needed. Metal is the new default renderer on these Macs; Vulkan and OpenGL are still under Graphics. Intel Macs stay on Vulkan.
Fixed the portable launcher on Windows never finding the game's crash reports, so Settings → Launcher can now copy them for a bug report.
Fixed game updates started from Steam filling the activity log with Steam overlay errors, which could also hide why a build failed.
Fixed a crash report on Linux and the Steam Deck when you closed the game with Stop in Steam.

changes: Online battles: two players' games play one battle, with both choosing their moves at the same time, from the launcher's Online tab. A Story party's Pokémon keep their moves, nature, stats, ability, held item, nickname and Poké Ball, at the battle's level.
Save anywhere: the menu you open with Start has a new SAVE option above EXIT. It saves where you stand, and Continue puts you back on that spot.
Randomizer: a new save can be a randomized run, and the save keeps its seed.
Rui and most trainers now have their detailed models in the field too, with sharper faces and real fingers.
Battle animations can run at any speed from 1× to 5× in steps of 0.1.
Macs with Apple Silicon: the game runs natively, and the wipe into a trainer battle plays in full instead of going black.
The game tells the launcher where you are, who you're battling and your lead Pokémon, for Show on Discord.
When Vulkan can't start on Linux, the game now tries the desktop's other window system before falling back to OpenGL, and the message says why Vulkan couldn't start.
In widescreen, the menu you open with Start now sits at the right edge of the screen, as it does in 4:3.
Fixed Pokémon getting a different nature and gender than a GameCube would give them at the same moment, which also threw off the random rolls after it, such as trainers' teams and damage.
Fixed the game not opening its window on Linux with newer graphics drivers, and that error calling the game Super Mario Sunshine.
Fixed people and objects disappearing near the sides of the screen in widescreen.
Fixed the arrow for picking a target sitting away from the status panels in widescreen.
Fixed the stripes of Yes/No boxes stopping short, and the Poké Ball in a text box's corner drawing outside the box, in widescreen.
Fixed Pokémon blinking twice as often at 60 fps, which also used up the game's random numbers faster than on a GameCube.

launcher: HD models: Wes uses his detailed model in the field. Turn it off under Graphics.
The game now builds from the port's own copy of the decompilation.

changes: Wes now has his detailed battle model while walking around, with a sharper face and real fingers.
Fixed the Pokémon faces missing from the Battle Now team screen.
Fixed opposing trainers misjudging a side's conditions and level-based moves.
Fixed the second trainer on a side being mistaken for the first.
Fixed Pokémon faces staying in memory after being replaced.
Fixed the Pokédex seen and caught flags on Linux and macOS.
Fixed Poké Ball catch rates on Linux and macOS.
Fixed the blue background on the main menus and save screen stopping short of the sides in widescreen.
Fixed the PC menus leaving black bars at the sides in widescreen.
Fixed the game crashing when entering a new area after playing for a long time.
Fixed Rui getting stuck walking on the spot when you first enter the mayor's house in Phenac City, and people stalling the same way in other cutscenes.

launcher: Battle animations: moves, send-outs and HP bars play at 2× speed by default. Change to normal speed or 4×, or skip them, under Gameplay.
Add to Steam: play from your Steam library, Big Picture or Game Mode, with artwork. Find it on the main screen, on Windows and Linux.
Skip Launcher: Steam can start the game straight away, and --play does the same from any shortcut.
Graphics presets: Low, Medium, High, Ultra and Steam Deck set the picture all at once. Find them under Graphics.
Crash reports: copy the newest report for a bug report, under Launcher. They stay on your computer.

changes: Fixed a box appearing around the white ring in some battle moves. Their ripple effect now works too.
Fixed your partner walking behind you facing the wrong way on Linux and macOS.
Fixed battle timers always showing 0 on Linux and macOS.
Fixed the title menu's selection jumping to the next option instead of sliding on Linux and macOS.
Fixed reflective effects not showing on Linux and macOS, along with the title options' animation and the stick in the P★DA.
Fixed items and Poké Balls saying they were meaningless to use in battle, and the bag jumping to another pocket afterwards.
Fixed shop messages showing the wrong price and item, like nearly 2 billion for one Super Potion. Sales always paid the right amount.
Fixed the game crashing when you pressed Down in the P★DA's Strategy Memo list.
Installing and updating the game downloads less: it no longer fetches two extra repositories to build.
Battle animations can run at 2× or 4× speed or be skipped, with menus at normal speed and text up long enough to read.
Building the game is faster: its code now compiles once instead of twice, on Windows too.
Setting up the game is quicker: the fixes its code needs now come ready-made instead of being worked out on your computer.
Game updates that change only part of the build now reuse more of what was already compiled.
The first game build after this update takes longer, as it starts over with what it keeps between builds.
Fixed new builds on Linux and macOS leaving out small corrections to battle and menu code that only a rebuild picked up.
Fixed the battle move menu showing the first move's PP and type whichever move you highlighted.
The logo movies at startup now fill a widescreen display with their background colour instead of black bars.

launcher: Fixed Windows builds with your own MSYS2, set with the COLO_MSYS2_ROOT environment variable, looking for the game's compiler in a folder that MSYS2 doesn't have.
Fixed a game download stopping at Prepare port source when a newer game commit is chosen under Settings, Manage game, Game source.
Windows builds now use a compiler that also runs on Windows 7, which the previous one could not.
The first game build on Windows after this update takes longer, as it starts over with the new compiler.

changes: Fixed builds reporting success when the game's compiler couldn't run: they now stop and say why.
Fixed a rare build that left out part of the battle menus' code.
Fixed Battle Now's party check overwriting nearby memory, which stopped the game on Arch Linux.
Fixed the game failing as it started when built on Arch Linux and other systems not based on Debian.
Fixed the game not fully unloading map code it had finished with.

launcher: New launcher background: a painted copper engine out in the desert.
Game updates and rebuilds are much faster: the launcher keeps what it compiled and reuses it. Free up space under Settings, Manage game clears it.
Import a Dolphin save: drop your North American .gci save on the Saves tab, or the folder it is in, and carry on from there. Your current saves are backed up first.
Join our Discord server: the Discord button at the top of the launcher opens the invite in your browser.

changes: The first build of the game is faster too.
Fixed the game stopping on macOS when you arrive in Phenac City with HD textures at the highest resolution.

launcher: First release: set up and play the Pokémon Colosseum PC port from your own North American disc on Windows, macOS and Linux.
Three-step setup downloads everything it needs and builds the game on your computer. The disc image never leaves it.
HD textures: all 7,498 of the game's textures upscaled 4×, on by default. Turn them off under Settings, Graphics.
Settings for the screen format, frame rate, picture sharpness, controls, rumble and GameCube controller adapters.
Your saves are backed up before and after you play. Restore one from the Saves tab.

changes: Native PC port with movies, music and sound, HD text, widescreen, 60 fps and Vulkan or OpenGL rendering.
